what_it_does: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) used for image recognition and object detection often need to run on resource-constrained hardware with very limited cache memory. This paper addresses the challenge of implementing sparse CNNs (neural networks where many weights are zero and pruned away) on such hardware by developing smarter memory management and cache strategies. The focus is on exploiting the sparsity (absence of weights) to reduce memory accesses and improve cache hit rates.
